overall: Atlanta is well into its evening cooling cycle as of 20:00 ET, with temperatures falling at -1.8°F/hr from a current reading of 77.0°F — well below the day's running max of 84.2°F, which was established around 17:00. The day featured a steady warm-up through the afternoon, peaking in the 82-84°F range before sunset-driven cooling took hold. High dewpoints (69.8°F) kept overnight lows elevated but did not suppress the afternoon peak significantly.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance was reasonably clustered, with GFS and HRRR both projecting 85.4°F, NBM at 84.1°F, and ECMWF at a slightly cooler 83.8°F. The observed running max of 84.2°F came in near the lower end of that range, closely matching ECMWF and NBM while falling about 1.2°F short of the GFS/HRRR consensus — suggesting the warmer models slightly overshot today's peak.
max_temp_prediction: With temperatures already 7.2°F below the running max and cooling at nearly 2°F/hr at 8 PM, there is essentially no path to exceeding 84.2°F tonight. The ensemble models further confirm this, with both assigning very low probabilities (5–14%) to outcomes in the 87–89°F range — well above what was observed. Today's daily high is locked in at 84.2°F with very high confidence.
